title: The Digestive System
seo_title: Primary 4 Science: Digestive System Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_text: Identify the organs of the human digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) and describe their functions. Recognise that digestion is the breakdown of food into simpler substances, which takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine, and that digested food is absorbed in the small intestine (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on the human digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small and large intestines, digestion and absorption. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Food is broken down so the body can use it.
body_html:
How to think about it

The digestive system breaks down food into simpler substances that the body can absorb.

mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → anus

  • Digestion happens in the mouth, stomach and small intestine, with digestive juices.
  • Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.
  • Water is absorbed in the large intestine. Undigested food leaves through the anus.
  • No digestion takes place in the gullet or the large intestine.
Example

Where does digestion start?

Teeth chew the food

Saliva starts to digest it

Answer: In the mouth.

Example

Where is digested food absorbed?

Digestion is completed in the small intestine

Digested food passes into the blood there

Answer: In the small intestine.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking digestion starts in the stomach. It starts in the mouth.
  • Thinking food is absorbed in the stomach. It is absorbed in the small intestine.
  • Thinking the large intestine digests food. It absorbs water.
  • Mixing up the order: the stomach comes before the small intestine.

faq.a: In the mouth, the stomach and the small intestine. No digestion takes place in the gullet or the large intestine.
In the small intestine. The digested food passes into the blood, which carries it around the body.

faq.q: What does the large intestine do?
faq.a: It absorbs water from the undigested food. The undigested food then leaves the body through the anus.

items.q: What is digestion?

Yes, digested food is absorbed here.

No. Only water is absorbed here.

Yes. Food is broken down here with the help of digestive juices.

items.q:

items.q: Which organ system works with the digestive system to carry digested food around the body?
items.e: The blood carries digested food.

items.q: Why should we drink enough water and eat fibre?
c: to help undigested food move through the large intestine easily
items.e: Fibre and water prevent constipation.

items.q: Which parts produce digestive juices?

the mouth, the stomach and the small intestine
items.e: Digestive juices break food down.

items.q: Why is the small intestine very long?
c: There is more time and surface for digested food to be absorbed.
items.e: A long small intestine absorbs more food.

items.q: Which statement about the large intestine is correct?
c: It connects the mouth to the stomach.
It digests most of the food.
It absorbs water from undigested food.
items.e: The large intestine does not digest food.

items.q: Which statement about the gullet is correct?
c: It moves food to the stomach by squeezing.
items.e: No digestion takes place in the gullet.

items.q:

items.e: Undigested food is stored here until it leaves the body.

items.q:

items.e: The blood carries digested food to the cells.

No. Water is absorbed here, but food is not digested.
Yes, it makes the most digestive juices.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine only.

items.q: Why is food in the large intestine more solid than food in the small intestine?
c: Water has been absorbed from it.
items.e: The large intestine absorbs water.

items.q: Ahmad ate a plate of chicken rice. Which part will his food reach last?
items.e: It reaches the large intestine before leaving the body.

items.q: Does digestion take place in the stomach?
c: No. Only water is absorbed here.
Yes. Food is broken down here with the help of digestive juices.
items.e: Digestion takes place in the mouth, stomach and small intestine.

items.q:

items.e: It squeezes food down; no digestion takes place here.

items.q: A pupil says that food is absorbed in the stomach. What is the correct idea?
c: Food is absorbed in the mouth.
Most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine.
Food is absorbed in the gullet.
items.e: The stomach only partly digests food.

items.q: Why should we not talk or laugh while swallowing?
c: Food will be digested too fast.
Food may go down the wrong way into the windpipe instead of the gullet.
items.e: The windpipe leads to the lungs.

items.q: Which part of the body is NOT part of the digestive system?
items.e: The heart is part of the circulatory system.

items.q: Where is digested food absorbed into the blood?
items.e: The small intestine is long and has a large surface.

items.q: Where is most water absorbed from undigested food?
items.e: The leftover food becomes more solid.

items.q: In which two parts does NO digestion take place?
c: the mouth and the small intestine
the gullet and the large intestine
the stomach and the small intestine
items.e: They do not produce digestive juices.

items.q: Where does digestion begin?
items.e: Teeth chew food and saliva starts to digest it.

items.q: Why is it important to chew food properly?
c: Smaller pieces are easier to swallow and digest.
items.e: Digestive juices work faster on small pieces.

items.q:
In which part of the digestive system does this happen?

items.e: Water is absorbed from the undigested food here.

items.q: Where is digestion completed?
items.e: Food is fully digested in the small intestine.

items.q: What is the job of the digestive system?
c: to break food down so the body can use it
items.e: Digestion.

items.q: How is the digestive system like a factory line?
c: Each part does a different job in turn to break down food.
Every part does the same job.
Only one part does all the work.
Food goes round and round in a circle.
items.e: The organs work together as a system.

items.q:
In which part of the digestive system does this happen?
Teeth chew food into smaller pieces and saliva makes it soft.
items.e: Teeth chew food into smaller pieces and saliva makes it soft.

items.q:
In which part of the digestive system does this happen?
It carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
items.e: It carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

items.q: Which part of the digestive system is the longest?
items.e: The small intestine is about 6 m long in an adult.

items.q: Which of these parts does NOT produce digestive juices?
items.e: The gullet only moves food to the stomach.

items.q: What happens to food in the large intestine?
c: Digested nutrients pass through its walls into the blood.
Solid waste (faeces) is stored until it leaves the body.
A muscular tube squeezes food down to the stomach.
Water is taken back into the body from the leftover waste.
items.e: The large intestine: Water is taken back into the body from the leftover waste.
